change_needed: Replace the sentence with: "The repeated header text order_item_id is itself one of the 25,833 'distinct IDs'; the footer's empty ID is NULL, which COUNT(DISTINCT) skips. So there are 25,832 real IDs."

change_needed: Add a boxed "Formula" panel for each measure, each followed by a symbol-by-symbol legend. (1) Before the first formula, add "Reading Σ": Σxᵢ means "add up every value"; i counts rows 1…n; n is the number of values. (2) Mean: x̄ = Σxᵢ / n (x̄ = "x-bar", the sample mean). (3) Variance: s² = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)² / (n − 1), with a line on why the deviations are squared (so they don't cancel) and why n − 1 (a sample slightly under-estimates spread; the sample mean is fitted to the same data). (4) SD: s = √s². (5) IQR = Q3 − Q1, defining Q1/Q3 as the 25th/75th percentiles. (6) CV = s / x̄. (7) z = (x − x̄) / s. (8) SE = s / √n in §21.8. where: §28.2 opener "Chapter 13 used WITH RECURSIVE once, to generate a list of months (section 13.8)."
issue: Known (M.7): Ch 13's recursive CTE (Pattern 5 MySQL note, §13.8, Answer 16) is being replaced by a calendar table. The reader now meets recursion for the first time here, and the first example is a 5-level, 35-row org chart. Several things are never taught in this chapter, because Ch 13's note carried them: what the keyword RECURSIVE does; that WITH RECURSIVE is written once and covers every CTE in the list, including non-recursive ones (relied on at the loop example and Answers 7 and 13); that column names and types come from the anchor; UNION ALL vs UNION; what "a pass" works on (the working table); and cte_max_recursion_depth (currently a Ch 13 key term).
change_needed: (1) Delete the opener sentence. Replace it with: "A recursive CTE is a CTE that refers to itself. It is how SQL walks data where rows point at other rows of the same table: org charts, product structures, account hierarchies." Cell 1: WITH RECURSIVE numbers AS (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM numbers WHERE n < 5) SELECT n FROM numbers;, with output 1–5 (5 rows). Explain line by line: RECURSIVE tells the database a CTE in this WITH list may refer to itself; it is written once, right after WITH, even when other CTEs in the list are not recursive. SELECT 1 AS n is the anchor: it runs once, and its column names and types fix the CTE's columns. UNION ALL glues each pass's rows onto the result. SELECT n + 1 FROM numbers WHERE n < 5 is the recursive part, and numbers inside it means only the rows the previous pass produced. The stop rule: when a pass returns no rows, the query ends. where: Q79-028: "A statistical test…gives you a real p-value" / "p = 0.000000"

With production-sized samples, trivial shifts become "significant": n = 200,000 per sample and a 0.03-SD mean shift give KS D = 0.012, p ≈ 2×10⁻¹³ (run). Ch 56 uses the KS statistic (effect size) with calibrated thresholds, not the p-value. "p = 0.000000" also hides the real value (about 10⁻⁴⁰ to 10⁻⁵⁷ across seeds).
change_needed: Change the hook: "'It looks a little different' isn't drift detection. A distance between two distributions (PSI, or the KS statistic D), with a threshold calibrated on a stable period, is." Show both the statistic and p, and add one sentence: "With thousands of rows, the p-value will call almost any difference significant; alert on the size of D or PSI, as Chapter 56, §56.8 does." Print p in scientific notation (f"{p:.1e}").

issue: Idempotent for duplicates, but not for corrections. DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM daily_summary WHERE total_revenue IS NULL OR total_revenue < 0) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'daily_summary check failed'; END IF; END $$; Explain each line, or run it from Python with assert count == 0 (Ch 47's data tests).
